slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: Creatinine forms a reddish complex with picrate in alkaline medium (Jaffé reaction); the colour intensity is proportional to the creatinine concentration in the sample.
The reading interval (30 and 90 seconds) is chosen to avoid most known interferences of the method — so the method is kinetic (two-point).
Creatinine is excreted by the kidneys; in progressive renal failure urea, creatinine and uric acid are retained in the blood.

slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “Creatinine-J” kit (IFU BSIS13-I, 07/11/22). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: serum or heparinised plasma — stable for 24 hours at 2–8 °C.
24-hour urine: dilute 1/50 with distilled water and multiply the result by 50; stable for 7 days at 2–8 °C.
R1 — picric acid 17.5 mmol/L; R2 — alkaline reagent (sodium hydroxide 0.29 mol/L); standard — creatinine 2 mg/dL (aqueous primary standard).

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Equipment: spectrophotometer or analyser reading at 492 nm (490–510), 1.0 cm cuvettes, stopwatch.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: Working reagent: mix equal volumes of R1 (picrate) and R2 (alkaline reagent).
Working reagent stability: 15 days at 2–8 °C or 7 days at room temperature (15–25 °C).
Store the kit at 2–8 °C protected from light until expiry. Signs of deterioration: particles, turbidity or blank absorbance at 492 nm ≥ 1.80.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: The standard (2 mg/dL) is easily contaminated — take it each time with a clean disposable tip.
IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: The values come from the SPINREACT “Creatinine-J” IFU (BSIS13-I). The IFU of the kit you use and the analyser manual always take precedence — check the programme against them.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 1. Conditions: wavelength 492 nm (490–510); temperature 37 °C or 15–25 °C.
2. Use a 1 cm cuvette; zero the instrument with distilled water.
3. Pipette into a cuvette: blank — working reagent 1.0 mL; standard — working reagent 1.0 mL + standard 100 µL; sample — working reagent 1.0 mL + sample 100 µL.
4. Mix and start the stopwatch.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 5. Read A1 30 seconds and A2 90 seconds after adding the sample.
6. Calculate ΔA = A2 − A1 for each cuvette (blank, standard, sample).

slides.title: Semi-automatic analyser: creatinine programme
rows: A1 — 30 s, A2 — 90 s (after adding the sample)

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: Creatinine (mg/dL) = (ΔA sample − ΔA blank) / (ΔA standard − ΔA blank) × 2 (standard concentration).
Conversion: mg/dL × 88.4 = µmol/L; for urine multiply by the dilution factor 50.
Linear up to 35 mg/dL; above that, dilute the sample 1/2 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 2.

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: IFU reference (serum/plasma): men 0.7–1.4 mg/dL (61.8–123.7 µmol/L), women 0.6–1.1 mg/dL (53.0–97.2 µmol/L).
Urine: 15–25 mg/kg/24 h; men 10–20, women 8–18 mg/kg/24 h.
These values are for orientation; each laboratory should establish its own reference range.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Haemoglobin (1 g/L) and bilirubin (55 mg/dL) interfere; lipids < 4 g/L do not.
Keep the reading times (30 and 90 s) and temperature exact — in a kinetic method a timing error changes the result directly.
IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.
Drugs and other interfering substances are listed in the literature (IFU — Young DS).
IFU: performance depends on the analyser used.

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Assayed control sera are run with each series (IFU: SPINTROL H Normal and Pathologic).
If a control falls outside its range, check the instrument, reagents and calibrator; do not release patient results.
Each laboratory sets its own quality-control scheme and the corrective actions when controls are out of tolerance.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: R2 (alkaline reagent): H314 — causes severe skin burns and eye damage; wear gloves and goggles.
Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
Used cuvettes, tubes and tips are disinfected.
